description: We are ASTRACARE, a team of six enthusiastic students passionate about technology, programming, innovation, and space exploration. We enjoy learning, sharing ideas, and solving real-world challenges through collaboration. We welcome curious and motivated people with skills in AI/ML, software development, data science, UI/UX, healthcare, space science, and research. You don't need to be an expert—just bring your creativity, commitment, and willingness to learn. Let's innovate together!
summary:
ASTRA HEALTH is health monitoring software for astronauts, built as a Flutter mobile app. It tracks five vital signs (heart rate, blood oxygen, temperature, blood pressure and respiration), refreshed every 3 seconds. A rule-based engine checks every reading and sets the crew’s status to Nominal, Caution or Attention. Warnings such as low oxygen, an unusual heart rate or fever are logged in an Emergency Center. Trend charts show how vitals change over time.

It addresses the challenge by giving crews a clear, real-time view of their own health. On long missions, help from Earth is far away: a message to Mars can take up to 22 minutes one way. Astronauts also face risks such as bone loss, cardiovascular changes and isolation, so early warning onboard matters. The prototype uses simulated data and illustrative thresholds. Next, we plan to connect real sensors and validate the thresholds against NASA research.
details:
What it does and how it works
ASTRA HEALTH is a mobile app that lets an astronaut see their own health status at a glance. A telemetry service generates a new reading every 3 seconds for heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO₂), temperature, blood pressure and respiration. A rule engine checks each reading. It flags low oxygen (below 94%, critical), an unusual heart rate (above 105 or below 55 BPM) and fever (38.0 °C or higher). It then sets the crew status to Nominal, Caution or Attention and logs each alert in an Emergency Center. The app has five screens: Mission, Vitals, Analytics, Alerts and Profile. The Analytics screen shows live trend charts for heart rate and oxygen.

Benefits and intended impact
On long missions, help from Earth can be minutes away (up to 22 minutes one way to Mars). ASTRA HEALTH gives crews early, onboard warning when vitals drift, so they can act sooner. It can support crew autonomy and mission safety. The same idea could later help remote and rural clinics on Earth.

Tools and technology
Flutter and Dart, Material 3 dark theme, ChangeNotifier for live updates, custom-painted charts, and Android Studio/IntelliJ. We tested the app on an Android phone. The code can also build for iOS and web. No special hardware is needed yet.

Creativity
We designed it like a mission-control console, with a status banner, color-coded alerts and a dark interface that is easy to read in low light. The charts are drawn by hand rather than from a library, so the app stays light.

What we considered
Clarity under stress, so one status shows first. Honesty about limits: the data is simulated and the thresholds are illustrative, not validated medical or NASA rules. Next steps are real wearable sensor data, thresholds checked against NASA research, personal baselines for each astronaut, and offline anomaly detection that syncs to ground control.
